strings.path.title: Funk Lines
strings.path.goal: Play sixteenth-note funk rhythm as single-note lines, two-note stabs and octaves, locked to a band, with the picking hand never stopping.
strings.path.assumes: You can play sixteenth notes with a click at 70 BPM and stop a note cleanly (the Intermediate Level of Rhythm Foundations covers both). A clean tone is the right one here. The minutes listed are one pass through the material; a groove is something you come back to for weeks.
strings.path.gradingLimits: The app times the notes it hears against where they are written, counts them, and checks single notes for pitch after the take. Two-note stabs and octaves are one attack each: timed and counted, never pitch-checked. The muted scratch strokes that funk players put between the notes are written as rests here. If the app hears one it counts as an extra note, so the bar on extras is loose, and how good your scratches sound is for your ear. Whether your notes were short enough is not measured either. None of this has been tried on a real guitar yet.
strings.path.skills.0: Sixteenth notes with a click at 70 BPM
strings.step.the-engine.title: The engine
strings.step.the-engine.goal: Keep the picking hand swinging in even sixteenths on one note, and put an accent where you choose.
strings.step.the-engine.why: Funk rhythm guitar is a hand that never stops: down, up, down, up, four times a beat, for the whole song. The part you hear is which of those strokes are allowed to sound. Before any are left out, the swing itself has to be even, and you have to be able to lean on any one of the four.
strings.step.the-engine.howTo.0: Sixteenths, counted '1 e and a'. Down on the number and the 'and', up on the 'e' and the 'a'. The motion comes from a loose wrist, as if shaking water off the hand.
strings.step.the-engine.howTo.1: Hold the pick lightly and let only its tip touch the string. A deep stroke is a slow stroke.
strings.step.the-engine.howTo.2: An accent is one stroke played a little harder. The others stay quiet, so the accent has something to stand out from.
strings.step.the-engine.payoff: One note that already grooves, because the accents fall on the backbeat.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-beat.title: Accent the beat
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-beat.purpose: Sixteen sixteenths on one note, the A at the D string's fret 7, with the first of every four accented.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-beat.howTo.0: Strict down-up. The accent is on the downstroke that starts each beat.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-beat.howTo.1: Keep the three notes after each accent clearly quieter. That contrast is the groove.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-beat.coachLin: I check that the accented notes were louder, roughly, and how even the sixteenths were.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-beat.detectio: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-and.title: Accent the 'and'
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-and.purpose: The same sixteen notes with the accent moved to the 'and' of every beat: still a downstroke, now halfway through the beat.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-and.howTo.0: Count '1 e AND a'. Tap your foot on the beat and play the accent between the taps.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-and.howTo.1: If the accent pulls the foot with it, slow down a rung. The foot stays on the beat.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-and.coachLine: The accent readout is rough: louder than the notes beside it or not. Trust your ear too.
strings.exercise.the-engine.on-the-and.detection: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.title: Accent two and four
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.purpose: Only two accents a bar, on beats 2 and 4, where the snare drum is. Everything else stays quiet and even.
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.howTo.0: Count the bar and lean on the first note of beat 2 and of beat 4.
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.howTo.1: Fourteen quiet notes and two loud ones. The quiet ones are the hard part.
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.coachLine: Two accents a bar is what I look for, on 2 and on 4.
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.the-engine.backbeat.detection.1: Accents are measured roughly, as louder than the notes either side. Compression and high gain flatten them.
strings.step.holes.title: Leaving strokes out
strings.step.holes.goal: Play three sixteenth-note figures, each with one stroke missing, while the hand keeps its full swing.
strings.step.holes.why: Take one stroke out of four and you have a figure. Take a different one out and you have another. The hand does exactly what it did before; on the missing stroke it passes over the string without touching it, or brushes muted strings for a scratch. Stopping the hand is what makes funk parts drag.
strings.step.holes.howTo.0: The hand swings in sixteenths the whole time. On a rest it misses the string, or plays a muted scratch: relax the fretting finger so the string is dead, and let the pick brush it.
strings.step.holes.howTo.1: Stop each note by relaxing the fretting finger without lifting it off the string. Short notes make the rhythm clear.
strings.step.holes.howTo.2: The last beat of each bar moves down two frets, from A to G, so you can hear where the bar ends.
strings.step.holes.payoff: Three one-bar grooves on two notes that are already funk.
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.title: One, and-a
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.purpose: A long note and two short ones on every beat: the 'e' is left out.
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.howTo.0: Count '1, and a'. Down, then down-up: the hand misses the string on the 'e'.
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.howTo.1: Three beats on A at fret 7, the last beat on G at fret 5.
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.coachLine: I time each note against where it is written, and check the two pitches after the take.
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.holes.no-e.selfCheck.0: Did the picking hand keep swinging in sixteenths through the rests?
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.title: One-e, a
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.purpose: Two notes, a hole, and one more: the 'and' is left out of every beat.
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.howTo.0: Count '1 e (and) a'. Down, up, miss, up.
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.howTo.1: Don't close the hole. The 'a' comes late, just before the next beat.
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.coachLine: A closed-up gap shows as early notes. I'll say how even it was.
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.holes.no-and.selfCheck.0: Did the picking hand keep swinging in sixteenths through the rests?
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.title: E-and-a
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.purpose: After a full first beat, every beat starts with silence and plays its other three sixteenths.
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.howTo.0: Count '1 e and a, (2) e and a, (3) e and a, (4) e and a'. On beats 2, 3 and 4 the downstroke on the beat plays the air.
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.howTo.1: Let the foot land in the hole. The first note comes straight after it, on an upstroke.
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.coachLine: The first note after each silent beat is the one I'd look at: early means the hole was cut short.
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.holes.no-one.selfCheck.0: Did the picking hand keep swinging in sixteenths through the rests?
strings.step.first-lines.title: Lines with the band
strings.step.first-lines.goal: Play two-bar single-note funk lines in A minor pentatonic over a band, with short notes and real silence between them.
strings.step.first-lines.why: A funk line is a handful of short notes placed around the drums. Most of the bar is silence, or scratches, and the notes that are there have to sit exactly in the gaps the kick and the snare leave. With a band behind you the test is simple: does it make you want to move.
strings.step.first-lines.howTo.0: Learn each line at the first rung with the count out loud, one beat at a time.
strings.step.first-lines.howTo.1: Everything is in the pentatonic box at the fifth fret, on the low three strings: first finger on the frets at 5, third finger on the 7s, little finger on the low E string's 8.
strings.step.first-lines.howTo.2: Play every note short. Listen to the hi-hat: it plays the same sixteenths your hand is swinging.
strings.step.first-lines.payoff: A four-bar single-note groove over a funk band.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-one.title: A line from the top
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-one.purpose: Two bars that start on the A at the D string's fret 7 and work down to the low A, mostly one note at a time with space around it.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-one.howTo.0: Bar 1 starts '1, and a' on the D string, then a single note on the 'e' of 2. Bar 2 starts the same way and ends on a held low A.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-one.howTo.1: The hand swings in sixteenths from the first note to the last.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-one.coachLine: Band on. I time your notes against it and check them after the take. Direct input or headphones make that fair.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Were the notes short, with silence between them?
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-two.title: A line from the bottom
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-two.purpose: The answer: two bars that start on the low A and climb to the A on the D string, where the first line began.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-two.howTo.0: Both bars start with the low A on beat 1 and the C at fret 8 on the 'a'. Bar 2 ends with two eighth notes and a held A.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-two.howTo.1: The low E string rings easily. Stop it with the fretting finger as soon as each note has spoken.
strings.exercise.first-lines.line-two.coachLine: Band on. I time your notes against it and check them after the take.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Were the notes short, with silence between them?
strings.exercise.first-lines.both-lines.title: Question and answer
strings.exercise.first-lines.both-lines.purpose: The two lines joined: four bars, down from the top and back up from the bottom.
strings.exercise.first-lines.both-lines.howTo.0: Bars 1 and 2 are the first line; bars 3 and 4 are the second.
strings.exercise.first-lines.both-lines.howTo.1: The held A at the end of bar 2 is your breath. Bar 3 starts on the same note.
strings.exercise.first-lines.both-lines.coachLin: This is the Step's test piece. I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.first-lines.both-lines.detectio: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.stabs.title: Two-note stabs
strings.step.stabs.goal: Hit two strings at once, short, on the backbeat, on the off-beats and on single sixteenths.
strings.step.stabs.why: Funk players rarely strum a whole chord. They take the top two or three notes of it and stab them, short and bright. Two notes at once need a stroke that crosses two strings and stops, and a fretting hand that kills both together.
strings.step.stabs.howTo.0: The stab is C and E: the G and B strings at fret 5, under the first finger laid flat. Those two notes belong to Am7 and to D9, which is why the shape works over both.
strings.step.stabs.howTo.1: Strike both strings with one small stroke and stop them at once by relaxing the finger.
strings.step.stabs.howTo.2: The low A on beat 1 is the first finger's tip on the low E string at fret 5: the same finger, moved across.
strings.step.stabs.payoff: A bass note and stabs that sound like a rhythm section by themselves.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-backbeat.title: Stabs on two and four
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-backbeat.purpose: The low A on beats 1 and 3, a short stab on beats 2 and 4. The simplest funk part there is.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-backbeat.howTo.0: Quarter notes on 1 and 3; the stab is an eighth note on 2 and on 4, with silence after it.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-backbeat.howTo.1: Make the stab half as long as the bass note.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-backbeat.coachLine: A stab is one attack to me: I time it and count it, and I don't check its pitch.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-backbeat.selfCheck.0: Were the notes short, with silence between them?
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-offbeat.title: Stabs on the 'and'
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-offbeat.purpose: The low A on beat 1, then a stab on the 'and' of every beat.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-offbeat.howTo.0: Count '1 and, (2) and, (3) and, (4) and'. With the hand swinging in sixteenths, every stab is a downstroke, halfway through the beat.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-offbeat.howTo.1: The foot taps every beat. After beat 1 the guitar plays only between the taps.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-offbeat.coachLine: I time each stab against where it is written. Whether your foot kept the beat is yours to say.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-offbeat.selfCheck.0: Were the notes short, with silence between them?
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-sixteenths.title: Stabs on single sixteenths
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-sixteenths.purpose: The low A on beat 1, then stabs scattered across the bar on single sixteenths, some on the 'and', some on the 'e' and the 'a', and one on beat 4.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-sixteenths.howTo.0: Learn it a beat at a time with the count. The hand swings in sixteenths and catches the two strings only where a stab is written.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-sixteenths.howTo.1: Stabs on the 'e' and the 'a' are upstrokes. Let them be as loud as the downstroke ones.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-sixteenths.coachLine: Six stabs and a bass note in the bar. I time each one.
strings.exercise.stabs.stab-sixteenths.selfCheck: Did the picking hand keep swinging in sixteenths through the rests?
strings.step.line-and-stab.title: Line and stab
strings.step.line-and-stab.goal: Play a bass-register line and answer it with stabs inside one bar, and move the part from Am7 to D9.
strings.step.line-and-stab.why: The classic funk guitar part is two players in one: a low line that talks to the bass, and stabs that talk to the snare. Putting them in one bar means the picking hand jumps from the low strings to the high ones between sixteenths, without the swing changing.
strings.step.line-and-stab.howTo.0: Low notes on the fingertips, with the little finger for the C at fret 8; stabs with the first finger laid flat across the G and B strings.
strings.step.line-and-stab.howTo.1: For D9 the stab moves up two frets, to fret 7: third and little fingers on the G and B strings. The bass note is D, the A string at fret 5.
strings.step.line-and-stab.howTo.2: Keep the swing small. The pick only travels as far as the next string it needs.
strings.step.line-and-stab.payoff: A two-chord vamp, Am7 to D9, with a line and stabs in every bar.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.call-and-stab.pur: One bar on Am7: three low notes, a stab, two more low notes, a stab.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.call-and-stab.how: Beat 1 is low A, a hole, C and A on the low E string. The stabs fall on the 'and' of beat 2 and of beat 4.
Stop the low string before each stab so the two don't ring together.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.call-and-stab.coa: I time every attack, low notes and stabs alike. Pitch is not checked when stabs are in the line.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.call-and-stab.det: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.call-and-stab.sel: Were the notes short, with silence between them?
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.am-to-d.title: Am7 to D9
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.am-to-d.purpose: A bar of each chord in eighth notes: the root, then stabs. For D9 the root is D on the A string and the stab is D and F# at fret 7.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.am-to-d.howTo.0: Both bars have the same rhythm: the root on 1, stabs on the 'and' of 1, the 'and' of 2 and the 'and' of 4.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.am-to-d.howTo.1: The hand does not move. Use the long rest in the middle of each bar to get the third and little fingers ready over fret 7, or the first finger back over fret 5.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.am-to-d.coachLine: I time every attack and say how even they were. The change of chord is where it slips.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.title: The vamp with the band
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.purpose: Two bars over a funk band: the line and stabs on Am7, then the same shape of part on D9, with F# in the line.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.howTo.0: Bar 2 starts on D, the A string at fret 5, and its stabs are at fret 7. The first finger reaches back to fret 4 on the D string for the F#.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.howTo.1: Listen to the snare on 2 and 4. Your stabs come just after it.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.coachLine: Band on. I time every attack against it.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.detection.0: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
strings.exercise.line-and-stab.vamp.detection.1: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.second-pair.title: The same shapes on Bm7 and E9
strings.step.second-pair.goal: Play stabs, and a line with stabs, over Bm7 and E9: the two stab shapes of the vamp, two frets higher. Then hold the two-bar vamp with the band, in B minor and in other keys.
strings.step.second-pair.why: The stab and the line are shapes, and shapes move. Two frets up the neck, Am7 and D9 become Bm7 and E9: the first finger's flat stab, the stab two frets above it for the second chord, and the same box of low notes, with one note a fret below it for the second chord. The line here is a new one, so the hand has to find its notes in the new place and cannot lean on what it memorised at fret 5.
strings.step.second-pair.howTo.0: Everything is two frets higher than on Am7 and D9. The low B is the low E string at fret 7. The Bm7 stab is D and F#: the G and B strings at fret 7, under the first finger laid flat.
strings.step.second-pair.howTo.1: For E9 the stab moves up two frets, to fret 9: third and little fingers on the G and B strings, E and G#. The bass note is E, the A string at fret 7.
strings.step.second-pair.howTo.2: The picking hand does what it has done all along: it swings in sixteenths, down on the beat and the 'and', up on the 'e' and the 'a', and passes over the strings on every rest.
strings.step.second-pair.payoff: The vamp in a second key, B minor, with a line and stabs in every bar, over the band.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-stabs.title: Stabs on Bm7 and E9
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-stabs.purpose: Four bars: the root on beats 1 and 3 with a stab on beats 2 and 4, a bar of Bm7 and a bar of E9, then the root on beat 1 with a stab on the 'and' of every beat, a bar of each chord again.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-stabs.howTo.0: Bars 1 and 2: quarter notes on beats 1 and 3, and the stab is an eighth note on 2 and on 4. Bars 3 and 4: the root on beat 1, then a stab on the 'and' of every beat. Count '1 and, (2) and, (3) and, (4) and'.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-stabs.howTo.1: Bars 1 and 3 are Bm7: the low B at fret 7 of the low E string, and the stab at fret 7. Bars 2 and 4 are E9: E at fret 7 of the A string, and the stab at fret 9.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-stabs.howTo.2: The first finger plays both roots. With the hand swinging in sixteenths, every attack here is a downstroke.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-stabs.coachLine: A stab is one attack: timed and counted, never pitch-checked. The change of chord is where the time slips.
Were the stabs short, with silence after each one?
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-line-stab.title: A line and a stab on Bm7
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-line-stab.purpos: One bar on Bm7: three low notes, a stab, three more low notes, a stab.
Beats 1 and 3 have the same rhythm: the beat, the 'and' and the 'a'. Beat 1 is B, B and D on the low E string, frets 7, 7 and 10. Beat 3 is E, F# and E on the A string, frets 7, 9 and 7. The stabs fall on the 'and' of beat 2 and of beat 4.
First finger on fret 7, little finger for the D at fret 10, third finger for the F# at fret 9.
Stop the low string before each stab so the two don't ring together.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-line-stab.coachL: Every attack is timed, low notes and stabs alike. Pitch is not checked when stabs are in the line.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-line-stab.detect: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-line-stab.selfCh: Were the stabs short, with silence after each one?
strings.exercise.second-pair.e9-line-stab.title: A line and a stab on E9
strings.exercise.second-pair.e9-line-stab.purpos: The same shape of bar on E9: E, E and F# on the A string, a stab, then G#, A and G# on the D string, a stab. G# is the third of E9, and the line leans on it.
The rhythm is the Bm7 bar's: the beat, the 'and' and the 'a' on beats 1 and 3, a stab on the 'and' of beat 2 and of beat 4.

The hand stays at fret 7. On the A string the first finger plays E at fret 7 and the third finger F# at fret 9. For the D string the first finger reaches back one fret: G# at fret 6, then the second finger plays A at fret 7.
The stab is E and G# at fret 9 of the G and B strings, third and little fingers.
strings.exercise.second-pair.e9-line-stab.coachL: Every attack is timed, low notes and stabs alike. Pitch is not checked when stabs are in the line.
strings.exercise.second-pair.e9-line-stab.detect: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.second-pair.e9-line-stab.selfCh: Were the stabs short, with silence after each one?
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.title: The second vamp with the band
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.purpose: Two bars over a funk band: the line and stabs on Bm7, then the line and stabs on the ninth chord.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.howTo.0: Bar 1 is the bar for the minor seventh chord and bar 2 is the bar for the ninth chord: the two line and stab bars of this Step, one after the other.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.howTo.1: The hand does not move between the bars. In bar 2 the first finger reaches back to fret 6 on the D string, in the sixteenth of rest after the stab on the 'and' of beat 2, and comes back to fret 7 for bar 1.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.howTo.2: Listen to the snare on beats 2 and 4. Your stabs come just after it.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.howTo.3: The frets, note names and chords here are for the first version, in B minor. Other Takes move the same part to another key.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.coachLine: Band on. Every attack is timed against it.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.detection.0: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.detection.1: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.second-pair.bm-vamp.variant.key: Two bars over a funk band: the line and stabs on Gm7, then the line and stabs on the ninth chord.

The hand does not move between the bars. In bar 2 the first finger reaches back to fret 2 on the D string, in the sixteenth of rest after the stab on the 'and' of beat 2, and comes back to fret 3 for bar 1.

Two bars over a funk band: the line and stabs on Dm7, then the line and stabs on the ninth chord.
Bar 1 is the bar for the minor seventh chord and bar 2 is the bar for the ninth chord: the two line and stab bars of this Step, one after the other.

The hand does not move between the bars. In bar 2 the first finger reaches back to fret 9 on the D string, in the sixteenth of rest after the stab on the 'and' of beat 2, and comes back to fret 10 for bar 1.
Listen to the snare on beats 2 and 4. Your stabs come just after it.
Two bars over a funk band: the line and stabs on Cm7, then the line and stabs on the ninth chord.
Bar 1 is the bar for the minor seventh chord and bar 2 is the bar for the ninth chord: the two line and stab bars of this Step, one after the other.

The hand does not move between the bars. In bar 2 the first finger reaches back to fret 7 on the D string, in the sixteenth of rest after the stab on the 'and' of beat 2, and comes back to fret 8 for bar 1.
Listen to the snare on beats 2 and 4. Your stabs come just after it.
strings.step.octaves.title: Octaves
strings.step.octaves.goal: Play a note and its octave together as one short attack, and move octave shapes in a sixteenth-note rhythm.
strings.step.octaves.why: An octave is the fattest single-note sound a guitar has, and disco and funk are full of it. The shape is two fingers with a string between them, and that middle string has to be dead: the first finger leans on it, so the pick can strike straight through all three.
strings.step.octaves.howTo.0: First finger on the low note, third finger two strings over and two frets up. Let the first finger lean back to touch the string in between.
strings.step.octaves.howTo.1: Strike through all three strings with one stroke. Only two of them sound.
strings.step.octaves.howTo.2: Stop the octave by relaxing both fingers together.
strings.step.octaves.payoff: A disco octave part that moves through three notes over a band.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-eighths.title: Octaves in eighths
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-eighths.purpose: A in octaves, low E string 5 with D string 7, and C in octaves three frets higher, in an eighth-note rhythm with rests.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-eighths.howTo.0: The shape slides up three frets for the C and back. Keep the fingers' spacing as it moves.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-eighths.howTo.1: Bar 2 ends on a held A.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-eighths.coachLin: An octave is one attack to me: I time it and count it.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-eighths.selfChec: Was the string between the two fingers silent?
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-sixteenths.title: Octaves in sixteenths
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-sixteenths.purpo: One octave, A, in the sixteenth-note figure of the first funk line: '1, and a', then the 'e' of the next beat, twice a bar.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-sixteenths.howTo: The hand swings in sixteenths across three strings now. Keep the stroke as small as the shape allows.
Squeeze for the note, relax for the rest. The fretting hand makes the rhythm as much as the pick does.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-sixteenths.coach: Eight attacks a bar. I time each one.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-sixteenths.detec: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-sixteenths.selfC: Did the picking hand keep swinging in sixteenths through the rests?
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.title: Octaves with the band
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.purpose: The same figure through three octaves over a band: a bar of A, then half a bar of D and half a bar of E, a string higher.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.howTo.0: D and E are on the A and G strings: frets 5 and 7 for D, 7 and 9 for E. The shape is the same.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.howTo.1: Move during the two sixteenths of rest at the end of each half bar.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.coachLine: Band on. I time every attack against it.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.detection.0: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
strings.exercise.octaves.octave-line.detection.1: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.displaced.title: Across the beat
strings.step.displaced.goal: Play figures that are three sixteenths long, and lines whose notes fall on the 'e' and the 'a', without losing the pulse.
strings.step.displaced.why: A three-sixteenth figure in a bar of four slides against the beat: it starts on the beat, then just before the next one, then halfway through one, then just after one. That rub is the sound of a lot of funk and Afrobeat guitar. The hand keeps its swing, the foot keeps the beat, and the figure moves between them.
strings.step.displaced.howTo.0: Tap the foot on every beat and do not let it follow the figure.
strings.step.displaced.howTo.1: Count the sixteenths in threes at the first rung: '1 2 3, 1 2 3'. Then feel it against the foot.
strings.step.displaced.howTo.2: The hand's strokes are unchanged: down, up, down, up. The figure starts on a downstroke one time and an upstroke the next.
strings.step.displaced.payoff: A two-note figure that rolls across the bar line of your foot and lands back on beat 1.
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.title: Two notes and a hole
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.purpose: A, G, rest, five times, and one more G to fill the bar: a three-sixteenth figure in a bar of sixteen.
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.howTo.0: The figure starts on beat 1, then on the 'a' of 1, the 'and' of 2, the 'e' of 3 and on beat 4.
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.howTo.1: The first figure and the last start on a beat. Everything between slides.
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.coachLine: I time each note against where it is written, and check the two pitches after the take.
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.displaced.threes.selfCheck.0: Did your foot stay on the beat while the figure moved?
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.title: Starting on the 'e'
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.purpose: A low A on beat 1, then pairs of notes on the 'e' and the 'a', answered by pairs on the next beat and its 'and': upstrokes and downstrokes in turn.
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.howTo.0: Learn it one beat at a time with the count out loud.
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.howTo.1: Upstroke notes are usually quieter. Make them match the downstroke that starts the bar.
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.coachLine: Four of these notes are on the 'e' and the 'a'. I'll say how even they were.
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.displaced.off-the-e.selfCheck.0: Did the picking hand keep swinging in sixteenths through the rests?
strings.exercise.displaced.long-phrase.title: A two-bar phrase
strings.exercise.displaced.long-phrase.purpose: A longer line in the pentatonic box whose rhythm keeps changing from beat to beat, ending on a held low A.
strings.exercise.displaced.long-phrase.howTo.0: Take it at the first rung until you can sing the rhythm.
strings.exercise.displaced.long-phrase.howTo.1: The held A at the end is the only long note. Everything before it is short.
strings.exercise.displaced.long-phrase.coachLine: This is the Step's test piece. I'll say how even it was and check the notes after the take.
strings.exercise.displaced.long-phrase.detection: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.displaced-shapes.title: Stabs and octaves across the beat
strings.step.displaced-shapes.goal: Play the three-sixteenth figure as stabs, play octaves on the 'e' and the 'a', and join a line that moves across the beat to stabs in one two-bar phrase.
strings.step.displaced-shapes.why: Moving a figure against the beat was learned on single notes. A stab crosses two strings and an octave crosses three, so the stroke is bigger, and an upstroke through two or three strings is the one that comes out thin or late. The fretting hand has nothing new here: the Am7 stab and the A octave, both with the first finger at fret 5. All of the attention can go to where the stroke lands.
strings.step.displaced-shapes.howTo.0: Foot on every beat, as before. The hand swings in sixteenths: down on the beat and the 'and', up on the 'e' and the 'a'.
strings.step.displaced-shapes.howTo.1: An upstroke meets the strings in the other order: the B string first for a stab, the D string first for an octave. Make it as loud and as short as a downstroke.
strings.step.displaced-shapes.howTo.2: The fretting hand makes the holes: squeeze for the attack, relax for the rest, with the fingers still touching the strings.
strings.step.displaced-shapes.payoff: A two-bar phrase over the band where a line that moves across the beat and stabs sit against a steady foot.
strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.stab-threes.pu: Stab, stab, rest, five times, and one more stab to fill the bar: the three-sixteenth figure, now on two strings.
strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.stab-threes.ho: The figure starts on beat 1, then on the 'a' of 1, the 'and' of 2, the 'e' of 3 and on beat 4, as it did with single notes.
The stab is C and E, the G and B strings at fret 5 under the first finger. It never moves: relax the finger for each hole.
The two stabs of a figure are down-up one time and up-down the next. Keep the two the same size.
strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.stab-threes.co: Eleven stabs in the bar, each one timed against where it is written. A stab is one attack, never pitch-checked.
strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.stab-threes.de: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.stab-threes.se: Did your foot stay on the beat while the figure moved?
strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.octave-off-the: The A octave on beat 1, then pairs of octaves on the 'e' and the 'a', answered by pairs on the next beat and its 'and': the rhythm of the line that started on the 'e', played with the octave shape.
Count '1 e (and) a, 2 (e) and (a), (3) e (and) a, 4 (e) and (a)'. Beat 3 is the only beat that starts with silence.
The octave is A: first finger on the low E string at fret 5, third finger on the D string at fret 7, the A string dead under the first finger. The shape does not move.
The octaves on the 'e' and the 'a' are upstrokes through three strings. Keep the stroke as small as the shape allows.
Nine attacks a bar, four of them on the 'e' and the 'a'. An octave is one attack: timed and counted.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.

strings.exercise.displaced-shapes.slide-and-stab: A line across the beat, with stabs

Two bars over a funk band. The two-note figure moves across the beat all through bar 1 and is answered by the same figure as stabs. Bar 2 starts on the low A, puts two notes on the 'e' and the 'a', and ends with two upstroke stabs and a held low A.
Bar 1: A, G, rest, four times, starting on beat 1, the 'a' of 1, the 'and' of 2 and the 'e' of 3. Then two stabs, on beat 4 and its 'e', where the fifth figure would start.
Bar 2: the low A on beat 1, the A on the D string on the 'e' and the 'a', G on beat 2, then silence until the stabs on the 'e' and the 'a' of beat 3. The held low A lands on beat 4.

Everything is at fret 5 and fret 7. The first finger lies flat across all six strings at fret 5 and stays there: it holds the stabs, the G and the low A, so only the pick has to travel. The third finger plays the A at fret 7 of the D string.
After the upstroke stab on the 'a' of beat 3 in bar 2, let the hand carry on up past the low E string, so that the downstroke on beat 4 starts above it. This is the widest the swing gets.
Band on. This is the Step's test piece: every attack is timed against the band. Pitch is not checked when stabs are in the line.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

strings.step.the-sixth.title: The Dorian sixth, and hammer-ons
strings.step.the-sixth.goal: Use F#, the note that turns a minor pentatonic line into a funk line, and hammer into notes inside a sixteenth-note rhythm.
strings.step.the-sixth.why: Funk in a minor key nearly always means Dorian. The note that matters is its major sixth, F# in the key of A, added to the minor pentatonic. It is the third of the D9 chord the band keeps going to, so playing it when that chord arrives makes the line and the harmony agree. A hammer-on into a note is the other small thing that makes a line sound spoken.
strings.step.the-sixth.howTo.0: F# is the D string at fret 4, one fret below the G. The first finger reaches back for it.
strings.step.the-sixth.howTo.1: A hammer-on here is two sixteenths from one stroke: pick the lower note, hammer the upper. The hand still swings, and misses the string for the hammered note.
strings.step.the-sixth.howTo.2: Aim F# at the bars where the chord is D9.
strings.step.the-sixth.payoff: A four-bar line over Am7 and D9 that could not be played with the pentatonic alone.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.sixth.title: A line with F#
strings.exercise.the-sixth.sixth.purpose: Two bars: the first funk line, which fits Am7, then an answer around D, E, F# and G that fits D9.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.sixth.howTo.0: Bar 2 starts on D, the A string at fret 5. Its F# is the D string at fret 4.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.sixth.howTo.1: The hand shifts back one fret for bar 2, or the first finger stretches. Either works at these tempos.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.sixth.coachLine: I time the notes and check them after the take. F# is the one I'm listening for.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.sixth.detection.0: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.title: Hammer into the note
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.purpose: G hammered to A on the D string, and D hammered to E on the A string, placed on different sixteenths of the bar.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.howTo.0: Pick fret 5 and hammer fret 7 with the third finger, as two even sixteenths.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.howTo.1: After some of the hammer-ons the upper note is picked again. That one is a separate stroke.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.coachLine: A hammer-on I can't hear costs nothing, so the picked notes carry the timing. Its volume is for your ear.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.detection.0: Hammer-ons, pull-offs and slides may be too quiet to detect. An unheard hammer-on or pull-off costs nothing. An unheard slid-to note still counts as missed today, so the bar here allows for it.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.hammered.detection.1: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.two-chord-line.title: Four bars over Am7 and D9
strings.exercise.the-sixth.two-chord-line.purpos: A line that follows the chords: pentatonic over the Am7 bars, F# in the D9 bars, with a hammer-on in bar 3 and a held D to end.
Bars 1 and 3 are over Am7 and start on A. Bars 2 and 4 are over D9 and start on D.
Bar 3 starts like bar 1. On beat 3 it stays on the D string: G hammered to A, then A picked again on the 'a'.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.two-chord-line.coachL: Band on. I time your notes against it and check them after the take.
strings.exercise.the-sixth.two-chord-line.detect: Hammer-ons, pull-offs and slides may be too quiet to detect. An unheard hammer-on or pull-off costs nothing. An unheard slid-to note still counts as missed today, so the bar here allows for it.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.step.the-pocket.title: The pocket
strings.step.the-pocket.goal: Hold a four-bar groove of lines, stabs and octaves over a band, and keep a one-bar line in the pocket for a full minute.
strings.step.the-pocket.why: A funk guitarist plays the same bar for five minutes and it has to feel better at the end than at the start. That is what 'the pocket' means: nothing rushes, nothing drags, every note is the same length it was last time. Long takes are the only way to practise it.
strings.step.the-pocket.howTo.0: For the minute, choose a rung where the line feels easy. The work is in keeping it identical.
strings.step.the-pocket.howTo.1: Listen to the band more than to yourself. If the groove feels good, your time is good.
strings.step.the-pocket.howTo.2: Stop at any pain in the hand, wrist or forearm. A tired forearm is one thing and pain is another; pain ends the set.
strings.step.the-pocket.payoff: A four-bar funk guitar part with everything in it, and a line you can sit on for as long as the band plays.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.title: Four bars of everything
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.purpose: A bar of line and stabs on Am7, a bar on D9, a bar of A in octaves, and a bar that starts in D octaves and walks up in single notes: D, E, F#, G.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.howTo.0: Each bar is one you have played: the vamp, then the octave figure. Bar 4 is half octaves, half single notes.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.howTo.1: The changes of register are the hard part. Look at the string you are going to.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.coachLine: Band on. I time every attack against it. Pitch is not checked when stabs and octaves are in the line.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.detection.0: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.groove.detection.1: At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.pocket-minute.title: One bar for a minute
strings.exercise.the-pocket.pocket-minute.purpos: The first bar of the first funk line, round and round over the band for sixty seconds.
Play it exactly the same every time: the same short notes, the same holes.
If your mind wanders, listen to the hi-hat and lock the hand's swing to it again.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.pocket-minute.coachL: I check that the time holds to the end of the minute. Whether every bar felt the same is for your ear.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.pocket-minute.detect: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.

Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.pocket-minute.selfCh: Did the last ten seconds feel as relaxed as the first ten?
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.title: Stabs for a minute
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.purpose: The off-beat stab part, a bass note and a stab on every 'and', for sixty seconds.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.howTo.0: Keep every stab the same length. They get longer when the hand tires.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.howTo.1: Breathe, and let the shoulder drop.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.coachLin: I check that the time holds to the end of the minute.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.detectio: Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.exercise.the-pocket.stab-minute.selfChec: Were the notes short, with silence between them?
strings.step.long-form.title: Eight bars and a change
strings.step.long-form.goal: Hold an eight-bar groove over a band, in B minor and in other keys, four bars of line and stabs and four bars of octaves, and keep its first bar in the pocket for a full minute.
strings.step.long-form.why: Songs are built from parts that last four or eight bars, and the guitar changes part when the song does. The change is where a groove comes apart: the last bar of one part rushes because the mind is already on the next. Eight bars with one change in the middle, in the key you moved the vamp to, is that problem at its smallest.
strings.step.long-form.howTo.0: Bars 1 to 4 are the Bm7 and E9 vamp, twice. Bars 5 to 8 are octaves: B for the Bm7 bars, E for the E9 bars, with four single notes at the end of bar 8 that walk back down to bar 1.
strings.step.long-form.howTo.1: The vamp is the one from 'The same shapes on Bm7 and E9'. The Bm7 bar, first finger at fret 7: B, B and D on the low E string, E, F# and E on the A string, stabs at fret 7. The E9 bar: E, E and F# on the A string, G#, A and G# on the D string with the first finger reaching back to fret 6, stabs at fret 9.
strings.step.long-form.howTo.2: Count the bars as well as the beats. Knowing you are in bar 4 is what makes the change arrive on time.
strings.step.long-form.howTo.3: For the minute, choose a rung where the bar feels easy. The work is in keeping it identical.
strings.step.long-form.howTo.4: Stop at any pain in the hand, wrist or forearm. A tired forearm is one thing and pain is another; pain ends the set.
strings.step.long-form.payoff: An eight-bar funk part in a second key with a change of part in the middle, and one bar of it held for a minute.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.title: Octaves over Bm7 and E9
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.purpose: Four bars of octaves over the band: B for the Bm7 bars and E for the E9 bars, in the sixteenth-note octave figure. The last bar plays the figure once, then four single notes that walk down toward the B.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.howTo.0: The B octave is the low E string at fret 7 with the D string at fret 9. The E octave is the A string at fret 7 with the G string at fret 9: the same shape one string over, with the first finger still at fret 7.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.howTo.1: Bars 1 to 3 are '1, and a', then the 'e' of 2, and the same again from beat 3. Change octave during the two sixteenths of rest that end each of them.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.howTo.2: Bar 4 plays the figure once, then F#, E, D and C#, short, on beat 3, its 'and', beat 4 and its 'and': the A string at frets 9 and 7, then the low E string at frets 10 and 9. Third finger, first finger, little finger, third finger.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.howTo.3: After the C# there is one sixteenth of rest before the B octave of bar 1: the third finger hops from the low E string to the D string, same fret.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-octaves.coachLine: Band on. An octave is one attack: every one is timed against the band and counted, and so are the four single notes. Pitch is not checked when octaves are in the line.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
Was the string between the two fingers silent?
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.title: The change of part
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.purpose: The join in the middle of the form, alone: the E9 bar of line and stabs, then a bar of B octaves.
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.howTo.0: Bar 1 is the E9 bar of the vamp. Its last stab is on the 'and' of beat 4, at fret 9.
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.howTo.1: Bar 2 starts with the B octave on beat 1: first finger on the low E string at fret 7, third finger on the D string at fret 9. In the sixteenth of rest before it, the first finger comes back from fret 6 to fret 7 of the low E string, and the third finger crosses from the G string to the D string at the same fret.
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.howTo.2: Look at the low E string during the last stab. The pick has further to travel than the fingers do.
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.howTo.3: When the loop comes round, the octave bar leads back into the E9 bar. That join is not in the form; the one to listen to is bar 1 into bar 2.
strings.exercise.long-form.the-change.coachLine: Every attack is timed. The first octave of bar 2 is the one to watch: late means the change took too long.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.title: Eight bars with the band
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.purpose: The whole form: four bars of line and stabs, then four bars of octaves over the same two chords, ending on the walk down that brings bar 1 round again.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.howTo.0: Bars 1 to 4 are the vamp twice. Bars 5 to 8 are the octave bars, with four single notes that walk down in the second half of bar 8.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.howTo.1: The octaves are B, E, B, then half a bar of E, and the walk down is F#, E, D, C#.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.howTo.2: The change comes after the stab on the 'and' of beat 4 in bar 4: the next attack is the first octave, on beat 1 of bar 5.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.howTo.3: Count the bars. The band will not tell you which half you are in: it plays the same two chords, one to a bar, all eight bars through.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.howTo.4: The frets, note names and chords here are for the first version, in B minor. Other Takes move the same part to another key.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.coachLine: Band on. Every attack is timed against it. Pitch is not checked when stabs and octaves are in the line.
With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.
strings.exercise.long-form.eight-bars.variant.ke: Bars 1 to 4 are the vamp twice. Bars 5 to 8 are the octave bars, with four single notes that walk down in the second half of bar 8.
The change comes after the stab on the 'and' of beat 4 in bar 4: the next attack is the first octave, on beat 1 of bar 5.

Bars 1 to 4 are the vamp twice. Bars 5 to 8 are the octave bars, with four single notes that walk down in the second half of bar 8.
The change comes after the stab on the 'and' of beat 4 in bar 4: the next attack is the first octave, on beat 1 of bar 5.
Count the bars. The band will not tell you which half you are in: it plays the same two chords, one to a bar, all eight bars through.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-pocket-minute.titl: The first bar for a minute
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-pocket-minute.purp: Bar 1 of the form, the line and stabs on Bm7, round and round over the band for sixty seconds.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-pocket-minute.howT: Play it exactly the same every time: the same short notes, the same holes, the stabs the same length.
The stabs are what change first when the hand tires: they get longer, or the one on the 'and' of beat 4 comes early. Listen to the snare just before each.
Breathe, and let the shoulder drop.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-pocket-minute.coac: The time has to hold to the end of the minute. Whether every bar felt the same is for your ear.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-pocket-minute.dete: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.
At this speed a real rig's input delay can push notes out of their matching window, which reads as late or missed. Evenness is the number to trust here, and only once the delay is calibrated.

Long unbroken playing, especially high-gain, can drown out where each note starts, so the app may stop hearing you. Unproven either way; if the app says it did not catch enough, believe that before you doubt your hands.
strings.exercise.long-form.bm-pocket-minute.self: Did the last ten seconds feel as relaxed as the first ten?
Were the stabs short, with silence after each one?
strings.level.beginner.title: Beginner: the hand that never stops
strings.level.beginner.summary: Even sixteenths with accents, the three one-hole figures, and two-bar lines over a band.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.0: You can play sixteenth notes with a click at 70 BPM.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.1: Your picking hand stops when the rhythm has a rest in it.
strings.level.beginner.startHereIf.2: You know the pentatonic box at the fifth fret, or can learn six notes of it.
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.swing-up.title: The swing up one string
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.swing-up.purpos: One, and-a on a single note of a minor scale, a note higher each bar on the D string. A different key each time.
Start well under your clean tempo. Down, down-up on every beat, first finger only, and move it up a note at each bar line.
strings.exercise.warmup-beginner.swing-up.coachL: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
strings.level.intermediate.title: Intermediate: stabs and octaves
strings.level.intermediate.summary: Two-note stabs on and off the beat, a line and stabs in one bar over Am7 and D9, a new line on the same shapes over Bm7 and E9, and octaves.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.0: You can play '1 e (and) a' and '(1) e and a' figures at 85 BPM with the hand swinging through the rests.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.1: You can play a two-bar single-note line over a band and keep the notes short.
strings.level.intermediate.startHereIf.2: Hitting two strings at once comes out late, or rings on.
strings.exercise.warmup-intermediate.hole-up.pur: One-e, a on a single note of a minor scale, a note higher each bar on the D string. A different key each time.
strings.exercise.warmup-intermediate.hole-up.how: Start well under your clean tempo. Down, up, miss, up on every beat, first finger only, and move it up a note at each bar line.
strings.exercise.warmup-intermediate.hole-up.coa: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
strings.level.advanced.title: Advanced: across the beat, and the pocket
strings.level.advanced.summary: Three-sixteenth figures and lines that start off the beat, as single notes and then as stabs and octaves, the Dorian sixth and hammer-ons, then a four-bar groove, a full minute, and an eight-bar form with a change of part.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.0: You can play a line and stabs in one bar at 80 BPM with a band.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.1: You can play octaves in a sixteenth-note rhythm with the middle string silent.
strings.level.advanced.startHereIf.2: Your parts work for 2 bars and drift over a whole song.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.threes-up.title: Threes up one string
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.threes-up.purpo: Two notes and a hole, five times a bar and one more note to fill it, on a single note of a minor scale, a note higher each bar on the D string. A different key each time.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.threes-up.howTo: Start well under your clean tempo. Foot on the beat while the figure slides across it; first finger only, and move it up a note at each bar line.
strings.exercise.warmup-advanced.threes-up.coach: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
